months_used: flat from March to November, jumps in the winter
identity: Very galloping and fair, basically flat
A slight rise (Rose Hill) about 10f from home
5f to 1m run on the straight course (the Lincoln is run here); a separate round-course mile starts in a chute
layout: A left-handed, galloping and almost level track; the only real gradient is a gentle climb over Rose Hill around ten furlongs out.
All races from five furlongs to a mile can be run on the straight course, with a separate one-mile start on the round course in a chute.
tactics: One of the fairest tracks in Britain: form from Doncaster tends to hold up well elsewhere.
On the straight course there is no strong side bias; winners come from the far side, the stands' rail and the middle.
Horses need to be good and genuine to win, but the course itself sets few traps.
ground: Good drainage means the ground is often good or quicker, and runners usually see their races out.
